newsitem.title: USA: Deflating Brent market punctures Louisiana crudes.
newsitem.headline: Deflating Brent market punctures Louisiana crudes.

text.p: U.S. crude prices started off weaker Thursday morning, while domestic grade differentials deflated on disappointing North Sea Brent markets.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was nearly steady, shading a few cents to the down side at $21.30-40 a barrel.
June/July WTI spreads returned to favor front month values, with the roll pegged at a six cents advantage to June.

Traders said confirmed deals were made for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at flat to benchmark WTI/Cushing. LLS had been tracking a premium to marker crude, but developments in the North Sea forced differentials lower.
The June Brent loading program scheduled the equivalent of 38.4 cargoes, down from the equivalent of 41.8 cargoes in May.
Traders were expecting an even lighter slate for June because of maintenance at many Brent-Ninian fields and a short month.
Other domestic grade talk had Midland/WTI at 34-30 cents under the marker, while Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire elicited offers at WTI/Cushing -45 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland ranged between a $1.42-38 discount, with Eugene Island around $1.65-50 under marker.
June WTI/Cushing Postings found favor at $2.05, traders said, a few cents firmer than late Wednesday.
